D001-D008_h001.question_both:
Well, doc, it’s been a rough patch lately. My wife, bless her heart, says I’m running myself ragged. I’m 59, been farming all my life, and keeping things in order used to be second nature. But now, I can’t seem to keep my thoughts straight. I'll start on one chore, then my mind jumps to something else, and before I know it, I've got three half-finished jobs and nothing done properly. Every little noise, every thought that pops into my head, pulls me away.

And the talking… I find myself just going on and on, can’t seem to stop. My wife just stares at me sometimes, probably wondering what's gotten into me. I’m always on the go, too. Can’t sit still for a minute, even when I'm exhausted. It feels like there’s a motor inside me, just pushing me forward, even when I don’t know where I’m going. This has been going on for a few months now, not always like this, but when it hits, it’s hard to settle down.
D001-D008_h001.question_a:
"Well, doc, everything just feels chaotic lately. My wife, bless her heart, says I’m always buzzing around like a fly in a jar, and I suppose she's right. I can’t seem to settle on one chore around the farm. I’ll start mending a fence, then my mind wanders remembering I need to check the irrigation, and next thing I know, I'm trying to fix a leak in the barn. Nothing ever gets fully done. And the chatter! I just can't seem to stop talking, even when I know folks are just nodding politely.

I’ve always been a bit like this, even as a boy, my mum used to say I had ants in my pants before I was even in school. Things have gotten a bit more intense recently, with these periods where I feel like I could conquer the world, full of ideas and energy, hardly needing any sleep. But even when I'm feeling this way, or when my mood is back to normal, these troubles with focusing and being constantly on the go are still there, every single day. It's not like the distractibility or the endless energy only pop up when I’m feeling really high; it’s a constant struggle."
D001-D008_h001.question_b:
Lately, things have been… a lot. My wife, bless her heart, says I'm like a tornado. I can't seem to stop moving; I'm always up earlier, pacing the farm, going over lists in my head. And those lists, they just grow and grow. I jump from wanting to fix the fence, to ordering a new tractor part, then to planning next year's crop rotation all in the same breath. It's like my mind is revving at 90 miles an hour, and I'm talking so fast, I can barely keep up with myself.

I've always been pretty organized on the farm, but lately, everything's a mess. I start on one task, and then some little thing – the sound of a bird, a thought about a tool – completely throws me off, and I'm on to something else entirely. It's driving me nuts because I feel so energized, like I could conquer the world, but nothing actually gets finished. This really only happens though when I get these high-energy spells. In between these times, I’m just my usual, steady self.

I try to organize files, but then an email pops up, or I remember I need to call a client back, and suddenly I’m down a rabbit hole of unrelated thoughts. I feel like I'm constantly moving, always needing to be doing something. My friends joke that I'm "driven by a motor" because I just can't sit still. It's exhilarating in a way, but also leaves me exhausted and wondering why I can't just… calm down.
D001-D008_h005.question_a:
It’s been a struggle, doctor. I feel like I'm constantly on a treadmill, but I can't quite get a grip on things. My desk is a disaster, and I’m always misplacing files – it's becoming a real problem with court deadlines. My mind just jumps from one thing to another, sometimes even in the middle of a conversation, I’ll get sidetracked by a thought about a new case or some minor detail. I try to listen, but then I'm off, thinking about something else entirely.

And I can’t seem to slow down. I'm always moving, always doing something. My colleagues joke I'm "driven by a motor," and it feels that way. I'm talking a mile a minute more often than not; I just can't seem to stop the words from coming out. There are times when I feel really high-energy, almost euphoric, and my thoughts race even more, but even when I’m not in one of those states, I still have trouble focusing and staying organized, and I’m still buzzing and talking excessively. This has been going on since I was a kid, long before I even knew what a "mood swing" was. It's just a constant part of how I am.

I can barely get a word in edgewise in conversations, just rattling on and on, bouncing from one idea to the next.

This whirlwind also makes it impossible to focus. My office is a mess; I can’t seem to organize my case files, and I find myself jumping between tasks, unable to complete anything because every little thing distracts me—even my own thoughts can pull me off track. It’s not how I usually am. This disorganization and distractibility? They only happen when I get into these incredibly energized, high-flying states, like I am now. When I'm feeling like my usual self, I'm sharp and focused. It’s definitely not a constant thing, just when I get like this. These intense shifts are really starting to disrupt my life.

D001-D008_h006.question_both: It’s been, well, I guess a few months now, that things have felt… different. I keep making silly mistakes around the house, like forgetting ingredients in a recipe or misplacing things I just had in my hand. My husband points it out, but it feels like my brain just jumps from one thing to the next. I can’t seem to settle on one chore without starting another, then another, and then nothing gets truly finished. Even when I try to sit down with the kids for a quiet activity, my mind is just buzzing, and I find myself interrupting them with my own thoughts, blurting things out before they’re even done talking. It's not like me, and honestly, it’s exhausting.
D001-D008_h006.question_a:
"Sometimes I just can't seem to focus, you know? Like, I'll be trying to help my son with his homework, and my mind just drifts off, completely missing what he's saying. Or I'll be making dinner and realize I've put in an ingredient twice because I wasn't paying attention. It's always been this way, even back in grade school, I remember my teachers saying I was 'daydreaming.'

It's not just the inattention, though. I have so much trouble just relaxing; I can't sit still to read a book or even watch TV. I’m always fidgeting, or needing to get up and do something. And my husband gets frustrated because I’ll blurt things out without thinking, interrupting him or changing the subject. Sometimes I get really irritable and energized, almost like I'm buzzing, and other times I’m so down. But even when I'm feeling really off, these issues with my attention and constantly needing to move or speak out of turn are still there, every single day, not just when my mood is swinging wildly."
D001-D008_h006.question_b:
Lately, I’ve been feeling so unlike myself. It’s been a whirlwind, really, and my husband is at his wit's end. There are these times, and honestly, they’ve been happening on and off for the past two months now, where I just can't focus on anything at all. I’ll be helping the kids with their homework, looking over their spelling, and suddenly I’ve made a silly mistake, like writing the wrong word down, or I’ll completely miss something obvious. Keeping track of one task, even simple household chores, feels impossible; my mind just jumps from one thing to another.

It's not just the inattention, though. During these times, I have this boundless energy. I can’t sit still for a minute, even when the kids are napping and I have a rare moment to myself – I can't just relax, I need to be doing something, anything. I also find myself interrupting people, just blurting out answers in conversation before they’ve even finished their sentence. It's embarrassing, but it feels like the words just spill out. This whole inability to focus and this restless energy, it all seems to hit me at the same time, when I’m also feeling incredibly high, thinking I can conquer the world, sleeping only a couple of hours and feeling completely rested. It’s like these attention and activity issues are entirely linked to when I’m in one of those incredibly revved-up phases.
